learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to predict and analyze the flight dynamic behavior of an aircraft based on geometric properties and independently derive and interpret the relevant equations for this.
They can name the safety requirements of a passenger aircraft and independently derive the safety budgets of individual aircraft systems.
They are able to predict the failure probability of a system, as well as an aircraft crash or maintenance incident, based on the system architecture.
Furthermore, they are able to optimize the safety level of an aircraft system through technical measures.

syllabus_topics: Safety and real-time requirements for avionics systems
Basic structure and functional principles of avionics systems
Mathematical models for calculating the failure probability of individual aircraft systems
Analysis methods for evaluating the effects of failure on the aircraft
Protection measures for avionics systems regarding environmental effects and random errors
Coordinate and reference systems of an aircraft

assessment_methods.method: Graded written exam (60 min) or graded oral exam (20 min) or graded presentation (20 min) for MABB611A
Graded written exam (60 min) or graded oral exam (20 min) or graded presentation (20 min) for MABB612A

assessment_rules: The module grade MABB640A is calculated from the grades of MABB611A and MABB612A with equal weighting. For each sub-component (MABB611A and MABB612A), the assessment can be a written exam, an oral exam, or a presentation.
bibliography: Stephen Corda; Introduction to Aerospace Engineering
Bernard Etkin, Dynamics of Atmospheric Flight
